title: Calibrating Pre-trained Language Classifiers on LLM-generated Noisy Labels via Iterative Refinement

problem.claim: LLM-generated labels can contain inaccuracies, and classifiers trained on noisy labels may overfit to that noise and suffer reduced generalization.

gap.claim: Learning from LLM-generated label noise has received less attention than learning from synthetic and real-world noise.

contributions.claim: SiDyP calibrates classifier predictions using simplex label diffusion with a dynamic prior.
SiDyP retrieves potential true-label candidates from neighborhood label distributions in text-embedding space and iteratively refines noisy candidates with a simplex diffusion model.
The authors make the code available on GitHub.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The framework increased the performance of a BERT classifier by an average of 7.21% on zero-shot LLM-generated noisy-label datasets and 7.30% on few-shot datasets.
The authors report extensive benchmarking across different LLMs and a variety of NLP tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Automatic label generation with open-source LLMs offers an alternative to labor-intensive and expensive manual annotation.
LLM-generated labels may be inaccurate, and noisy-label training can harm model generalization through overfitting.
Prior noisy-label studies have focused mainly on synthetic and real-world noise, leaving LLM-generated label noise less studied.
SiDyP uses neighborhood label distributions in text-embedding space and iterative simplex diffusion to refine noisy candidates and calibrate predictions.
The authors report average performance gains for BERT on zero-shot and few-shot datasets and benchmarking across LLMs and NLP tasks.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework refines noisy label candidates using neighborhood information in text-embedding space and iterative diffusion.

interpretation.claim: Representing local label structure may help reduce the impact of automatically generated label noise.

application.claim: For NLP systems trained on LLM-generated labels, consider neighborhood-based candidate retrieval followed by iterative label refinement before classifier calibration.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which tasks, noise conditions, or dataset characteristics may limit this approach.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the benchmark datasets, NLP tasks, LLMs, baselines, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not describe the simplex diffusion formulation, dynamic prior, or refinement schedule.
The abstract does not define whether the reported percentage gains are relative or absolute.
